gita.name: Bhagavad Gita
gita.intro: The Bhagavad Gita is a 700-verse Hindu scripture that is part of the epic Mahabharata. It is a narrative framework of a dialogue between Pandava prince Arjuna and his guide and charioteer Krishna.

lessons.title: Observing the Armies
lessons.content: Arjuna is overcome with sorrow and confusion as he sees his relatives and teachers in the opposing army. He questions the righteousness of war.

lessons.title: Sankhya Yoga (Contents of the Gita Summarized)
lessons.content: Krishna begins his teachings, explaining the eternal nature of the soul (Atman) and the temporary nature of the material body. He introduces Karma Yoga (selfless action).

lessons.title: The Core of Karma Yoga
lessons.sanskrit:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
lessons.content: You have a right to perform your prescribed duty, but you are not entitled to the fruits of action. Never consider yourself the cause of the results of your activities, and never be attached to not doing your duty.

lessons.title: The Eternal Soul
lessons.sanskrit:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही॥
lessons.content: As a person puts on new garments, giving up old ones, the soul similarly accepts new material bodies, giving up the old and useless ones.

lessons.title: Karma Yoga
lessons.content: Krishna explains that nobody can remain inactive even for a moment. One must perform duties without attachment to the results.

lessons.title: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
lessons.content: Krishna reveals that he descends to earth whenever righteousness declines (Yada Yada Hi Dharmasya) to protect the good and destroy evil.

lessons.title: Descent of the Divine
lessons.sanskrit:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम्॥
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे॥
lessons.content: Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice, O descendant of Bharata, and a predominant rise of irreligion—at that time I descend Myself. To deliver the pious and to annihilate the miscreants, as well as to reestablish the principles of religion, I Myself appear, millennium after millennium.

lessons.title: Dhyana Yoga
lessons.content: Focuses on the practice of meditation. Controlling the restless mind is difficult, but it can be achieved by constant practice and detachment.

lessons.title: The Universal Form
lessons.content: Krishna reveals his Vishvarupa (Universal Form) to Arjuna, showing that all beings, planets, and the entire cosmos exist within Him.

lessons.title: Conclusion - Perfection of Renunciation
lessons.content: The ultimate surrender. Krishna tells Arjuna to abandon all varieties of religion and simply surrender unto Him.

lessons.title: The Ultimate Surrender
lessons.sanskrit:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज।
अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः॥
lessons.content: Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.

shivpurana.name: Shiv Mahapurana
shivpurana.intro: The Shiva Purana is one of the eighteen major Puranas of Hinduism. It centers around the Hindu god Shiva and goddess Parvati, containing extensive cosmology, mythology, and philosophy.

lessons.title: The Origin of the Lingam
lessons.content: The Purana begins with the story of Brahma and Vishnu arguing over who is supreme. An infinite pillar of fire (Jyotirlinga) appears, representing Shiva as the supreme consciousness without beginning or end.

lessons.title: The Birth of Kartikeya
lessons.content: Describes the marriage of Shiva and Parvati, and the birth of Lord Kartikeya, who was destined to defeat the demon Tarkasur.

lessons.title: The 12 Jyotirlingas
lessons.content: The text describes the twelve sacred shrines of Shiva (Somnath, Mallikarjuna, Mahakaleshwar, Omkareshwar, Kedarnath, Bhimashankar, Kashi Vishwanath, Trimbakeshwar, Vaidyanath, Nageshwar, Rameshwar, and Grishneshwar) and the merit of visiting them.

lessons.title: Devotion and Asceticism
lessons.content: Emphasizes that true devotion to Shiva does not require wealth or elaborate rituals, but a pure heart and simple offerings like Bilva leaves and water.

vedas.name: The Vedas
vedas.intro: The Vedas are a large body of religious texts originating in ancient India. Composed in Vedic Sanskrit, the texts constitute the oldest layer of Sanskrit literature and the oldest scriptures of Hinduism.

lessons.title: The Truth is One
lessons.content: Ekam sat vipra bahudha vadanti - Truth is one, but the wise speak of it in many ways. This establishes the underlying unity of all divine manifestations.

lessons.title: Aham Brahmasmi (Brihadaranyaka Upanishad)
lessons.content: I am Brahman. This profound statement indicates the identity of the individual soul (Atman) with the universal absolute (Brahman).

lessons.title: Tat Tvam Asi (Chandogya Upanishad)
lessons.content: Thou Art That. Meaning that the true self within you is the same as the ultimate reality of the universe.

lessons.title: Gayatri Mantra
lessons.sanskrit:
ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः।
तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि।
धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात्॥
lessons.content: We meditate upon the spiritual effulgence of that adorable supreme divine reality, who is the source of the physical, astral and heavenly spheres of existence. May that supreme divine being enlighten our intellect.
